themes_detail.label: Noise Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints skyrocketed 470% THIS WEEK to 109 complaints vs. a baseline average of 19.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks, representing the most acute single-week spike in the district and suggesting either a specific noise source or event triggering widespread resident frustration.
evidence: 109 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (470% spike, z-score: 9.35)
Highest z-score among all active spikes, indicating most statistically anomalous event
Noise-Residential (2620 complaints, 90-day total) and Noise-Street/Sidewalk (2364 complaints, 90-day total) are top complaint categories district-wide
reporting_angles: Investigate what triggered this specific spike—construction project, event, or new noise source in a particular neighborhood block
Interview residents and 311 callers to identify common complaints and affected areas within the district

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped 233% THIS WEEK to 5 complaints vs. a baseline average of 1.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks, potentially signaling new illegal or non-compliant cannabis operations opening in the district or existing operations expanding their footprint.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (233% spike, z-score: 4.95)
Spike aligns with broader city enforcement period on unlicensed retail cannabis operations
No prior local news coverage or community board agenda items flagging this issue
reporting_angles: Map the 5 complaints to identify hotspot neighborhoods and address patterns of illegal or non-compliant retail operations
Contact NYPD Narcotics or Department of Finance to verify enforcement activity and licensing status of flagged retailers

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Complaints Plummet
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints DROPPED 64% THIS WEEK to 37 complaints vs. a baseline average of 101.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: -6.96), a statistically significant and unusual decline that may indicate either a reporting lag, a resolved systemic issue, or a temporary gap in service requests.
evidence: 37 plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 101.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (64% decline, z-score: -6.96)
Plumbing is 7th-most-common complaint type district-wide (1193 complaints over 90 days), so decline is material
Inverse pattern to broader trends suggests data collection or reporting issue rather than real improvement
reporting_angles: Verify with 311 whether reporting or processing delays explain the sudden decline
Check if a major plumbing repair initiative or contractor deployment occurred in the district this week

themes_detail.label: Graffiti & Street Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged 540% three weeks ago to 4 complaints vs. a baseline average of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks, coinciding with elevated rodent complaints (120% spike, 22 complaints three weeks ago) and suggesting a broader deterioration in street conditions and neighborhood maintenance.
evidence: Graffiti complaints UP 540% three weeks ago (4 vs. 0.6 baseline, z-score: 4.85)
Rodent complaints UP 120% three weeks ago (22 vs. 10.0 baseline, z-score: 3.89)
Convergence of two infrastructure/sanitation spikes suggests either a specific neighborhood block neglected or a Sanitation service gap
reporting_angles: Canvass the neighborhoods with highest graffiti and rodent concentrations three weeks ago to see if conditions have improved or worsened since
Interview Sanitation Department about any staffing or scheduling changes that may have created a service gap in early reporting period

themes_detail.label: Bike/Roller/Skate Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Bike, roller, and skateboard complaints spiked 2300% three weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline average), the second-highest z-score anomaly in the data, suggesting a specific street event, skateboard plaza activity, or new bike lane usage pattern that generated concentrated resident complaints.
evidence: 3 bike/roller/skate complaints three weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Spike is temporally distinct and isolated; no sustained elevated baseline suggests one-off event or location
No community board or Reddit discussion corroborating this activity, limiting context
reporting_angles: Identify the specific street or park location where the three complaints were filed to determine if a new skate spot, bike lane, or youth gathering area emerged
Interview Parks or Transportation to verify if any new bike infrastructure or event permits were issued around that timeframe
